# RPC Mode

<!-- This file is generated from TypeScript source. Do not edit it manually; run yarn run generate:references. -->

`octocode --mode rpc` runs one headless session controlled over stdin and stdout. Use it to embed Octocode in another program; see [CLI modes](cli.md) for the other modes. SDK users can call the typed `RpcClient`, which spawns the process and wraps these commands.

Each line on stdin is one JSON command, and each line on stdout is one JSON record. Framing is LF only: split on `\n`, not on other Unicode line separators, which may appear inside strings. Octocode refuses `@file` arguments in this mode. It takes over stdout for protocol records and redirects other stdout writes to stderr.

## Protocol

The first record of every session is `{"type":"rpc_ready","protocolVersion":1,"version":"…","sessionId":"…"}`. `protocolVersion` changes only when a change would break an existing driver; `version` is the Octocode version. `get_state` repeats both. Commands sent before startup finishes are held, so a driver need not wait for this record. The `RpcClient` passes it to its `onReady` option, and its `start()` resolves when this record arrives. It rejects if the process exits, fails to start, is stopped, or exceeds `startupTimeoutMs` (default 60,000 ms; an integer from 1 to 2,147,483,647). On a startup timeout, it stops the worker before rejecting and includes the bounded stderr tail in the error.

Every command has a `type` and an optional string `id`. A response repeats the `id` and names the `command` it answers:

- Success: `{"type":"response","command":"get_state","success":true,"data":{...}}`. `data` is omitted for commands that return nothing.
- Failure: `{"type":"response","command":"…","success":false,"error":"…"}`. A line that is not JSON answers with `command: "parse"`; an unknown or malformed command answers with its `type` and names the field at fault. A failure with no `id`, such as a `parse` answer, cannot be tied to a command; the `RpcClient` passes it to its `onProtocolError` option and names it in that command's timeout. A `prompt` refused because the model has no usable credentials also carries `authRequired: true`.
- `prompt` answers as soon as the input is accepted (`data.disposition`); it does not wait for the run. Follow progress through events, or set `waitForCompletion` to answer after the run, in which case a busy session replies with `execution: "not-sent"` and sends nothing. The answer's `data.outcome` says how the prompt's run ended: `status` is `completed`, `failed`, `aborted` or `truncated`, with `stopReason`, `errorMessage` and the run's cumulative `usage`; a prompt that ran no model, such as a command, answers without it. A failed run still answers `success: true`, because the command itself succeeded, and so does a run stopped by `abort` (`status: "aborted"`). A prompt stopped before it was accepted answers `disposition: "not-sent"` with an `aborted` outcome and zero usage: it started no run. `agent_settled` carries the same `outcome`, so a driver need not fold `message_end` events. A failure raised after an accepted prompt without `waitForCompletion` arrives as a `{"type":"run_error","id":...,"error":...}` record.
- A `prompt` that starts with a built-in slash command (`/context`, `/btw`, `/diff`, `/compact`, `/settings` and the other built-in commands; RPC has dedicated commands for some, such as `compact`) fails with `error: "/<name> is available in the interactive terminal only."`; `get_commands` lists only extension commands, prompt templates and skills.
- A native command a `prompt` runs that fails answers `success: false` with its error, beside the `extension_error` event (`event: "command"`). Commands that succeed answer `disposition: "handled"`.

Session events stream as they occur, without a request: `agent_start`, `turn_start`, `message_start`, `message_update`, `message_end`, `tool_execution_start`, `tool_execution_update`, `tool_execution_end`, `turn_end`, `agent_end` and `agent_settled`, plus `queue_update`, `compaction_start`, `compaction_end`, `auto_retry_start`, `auto_retry_end`, `model_wait` and other session records. `model_wait` says a model request has sent nothing for `idleMs` milliseconds: it arrives once the request has been quiet for 20 s, counted from when the request went out (a compaction before it does not count), is refreshed every 5 s, and carries `idleMs: 0` when the model answers or the request ends. Streaming `message_update` events carry only the delta and the cumulative `usage`; the finished message arrives in `message_end`. While a stdout write is pending, only the latest `tool_execution_update` of each call is kept, since each is a whole snapshot; a slow reader sees fewer updates, and never one after the call's end. Each `tool_execution_start`, `tool_execution_update` and `tool_execution_end` also carries `display`: how the call reads (title, summary, outcome and ordered blocks), built by the tool's `display()` or the generic display, the same data the terminal, web view, HTML export and ACP draw. It is for people; `args`, `partialResult` and `result` stay the model-facing data.

By default each event is whole, so one tool result travels up to five times: in `tool_execution_end`, its `message_start` and `message_end`, `turn_end` and `agent_end`, each time with its `structuredContent` (a bash result's holds up to 1 MiB). Assistant messages never carry `requestTrace` on the wire: it lists every layer of the request, and the session file keeps it. A driver that does not need the copies starts the process with `--rpc-lean-events`; a subagent's parent always does. Then `tool_execution_end` carries the result without `structuredContent`, a tool result's `message_start` and `message_end` carry the message without `content`, `details` and `structuredContent` (match it to `tool_execution_end` by `toolCallId`), a `message_update` that ends a block (`text_end`, `thinking_end`, `toolcall_end`) has no `content` or `toolCall` (the deltas built it and `message_end` carries it), and `turn_end` and `agent_end` refer to each message by `role` and `timestamp`, plus `toolCallId`, `toolName`, `isError` and `stopReason` when it has them. User and custom messages and every other event are unchanged.

Dialogs and status updates arrive as `extension_ui_request` records (`select`, `confirm`, `input`, `editor`, `notify`, `setStatus`, `setWidget`, `setTitle`, `set_editor_text`). Answer `select`, `confirm`, `input` and `editor` with an `extension_ui_response` line carrying the request `id` and a `value`, `confirmed` or `cancelled: true`. A `select` request from a client without `--rpc-ask` carries `approval: true` when the dialog decides whether to allow an action (every permission prompt), with that prompt's `permission` and `ask` card; show it as an approval. A `confirm` request never does. A client started with `--rpc-ask` also gets the `ask` method: one request carries `questions`, a batch of typed questions (`text`, `choice`, `multi`, `confirm` or `approval`, each with an `id`, its `options` and their `role`), plus `approval: true` when a question is a permission prompt and `timeout` in milliseconds. An approval from a subagent also carries `header`, a line for its parent to read and never show. Answer with an `extension_ui_response` carrying the request `id` and `replies`, one per question: `{ id, picks }` (option ids, plus `text` for a typed answer or write-in) or `{ id, cancelled }` (`declined`, `aborted`, `unavailable` or `timeout`). A question may carry `timeoutSeconds`: when it runs out the host takes the options marked `recommended`, closes the dialog with `extension_ui_dismiss` and treats them as answered; a client that fills in the defaults itself marks its reply `auto: true`. A reply that picks an option the question does not offer declines the whole batch, and `cancelled: true` declines it too. Without `--rpc-ask` the process never sends `ask`: the same questions arrive as `select`, `confirm` and `input`. A dialog can end without your response: another client answered it, its run was aborted, or its timeout passed. Octocode then emits an `extension_ui_dismiss` record carrying that request's `id`; close that dialog, because a response sent for it afterwards is ignored. The Octocode `RpcClient` passes the id to its `onExtensionUIDismiss` option. Failures in a command or hook arrive as `extension_error`. A `setStatus` record carries `statusKey`, plain `statusText` (absent to clear) and, when one was given, `statusTone` (`accent`, `muted`, `dim`, `success`, `warning` or `error`) for the client to colour in its own palette.

A dialog blocks its run until it is answered, with no timeout. A driver that answers nothing should start the process with `--no-dialogs`. The session then runs with no UI, as a print run does: a permission ask gets the same refusal, with its reason, and no `extension_ui_request` records are emitted, including `notify` and `setStatus`.

The process exits when stdin closes, on `SIGINT` (exit 130), `SIGTERM` (143) or `SIGHUP` (129; `SIGHUP` is not available on Windows), or after an extension requests shutdown. Pending extension requests are cancelled first. These do not wait for a run: closing stdin aborts the current run and exits 0, even if a command sent just before it never ran, so a driver that needs the result keeps stdin open until `agent_settled` or the `waitForCompletion` answer arrives. A requested shutdown waits for the current run to settle.

If a write to stdout fails because the driver closed its end, the session is released and the process exits 1 with one line on stderr; a closed stdout is noticed at the next write. In the default `full` permission mode the process says on stderr at session start that most actions run without asking, that browser cookies and other explicit approval requirements still apply, and where actions are recorded.

## Commands

| Command | Fields | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `prompt` | `message`: string<br>`images?`: object[]<br>`streamingBehavior?`: "steer" \| "followUp"<br>`waitForCompletion?`: boolean<br>`dispatchId?`: string | Send a message. During a run, `streamingBehavior` queues it as `steer` or `followUp`. `dispatchId` correlates extension-dispatched work when `waitForCompletion` is set. |
| `steer` | `message`: string<br>`images?`: object[]<br>`toolChoice?`: "none" | Queue a message delivered while the agent is running. On an idle session it still answers `queued` and starts nothing: it waits for the next prompt. To avoid that race at the end of a run, send `prompt` with `streamingBehavior`. |
| `follow_up` | `message`: string<br>`images?`: object[] | Queue a message for after the agent stops. On an idle session it answers `queued` and starts nothing, as `steer` does. |
| `abort` | `holdShutdown?`: true | Stop the current run. For terminal shutdown preparation, `holdShutdown: true` keeps extension-requested graceful exit pending until stdin closes, so the caller can capture descendant ownership after work stops. This cannot be undone: later commands other than `abort` are rejected; pending responses and extension UI replies still complete. EOF, termination signals and parent-loss cleanup remain active. Omit the field for ordinary abort. |
| `clear_queue` |  | Drop all queued steering and follow-up messages; returns what was dropped. |
| `get_queue` |  | List queued inputs with their `queueId` values. |
| `edit_queued` | `queueId`: string<br>`text`: string | Replace the text of a queued input; `data.outcome` is `replaced`, `removed` or `missing`. |
| `remove_queued` | `queueId`: string | Remove one queued input. |
| `move_queued` | `queueId`: string<br>`direction`: "up" \| "down" | Move a queued input up or down. |
| `new_session` | `parentSession?`: string | Start a new session, optionally linked to a parent session file. |
| `plan` | `action`: "show" \| "enter" \| "leave" \| "approve"<br>`revision?`: integer | Show, enter, leave or approve plan mode; `revision` pins the plan revision to approve. |
| `get_state` |  | Protocol and Octocode versions, model, thinking level, streaming and compaction flags, queue modes, session identity and message counts. |
| `set_model` | `provider`: string<br>`modelId`: string | Select a model by provider and ID from the available models; fails if it is not available. |
| `cycle_model` |  | Switch to the next model; `data` is `null` when there is nothing to cycle. |
| `get_available_models` |  | List the available models. A model whose plan allows interactive use only carries `interactiveOnly: true`. |
| `set_thinking_level` | `level`: "off" \| "minimal" \| "low" \| "medium" \| "high" \| "xhigh" \| "max" | Set the thinking level. |
| `cycle_thinking_level` |  | Switch to the next thinking level the model supports. |
| `get_available_thinking_levels` |  | List the levels the current model supports. |
| `set_steering_mode` | `mode`: "all" \| "one-at-a-time" | Deliver queued steering messages `all` at once or `one-at-a-time`. |
| `set_follow_up_mode` | `mode`: "all" \| "one-at-a-time" | Deliver queued follow-up messages `all` at once or `one-at-a-time`. |
| `compact` | `customInstructions?`: string | Run compaction now; `customInstructions` is limited in length by the schema. |
| `set_auto_retry` | `enabled`: boolean | Enable or disable automatic retry of transient failures for this session. Settings files are not changed, and a new session starts from settings again. |
| `abort_retry` |  | Cancel a pending automatic retry wait. |
| `bash` | `command`: string<br>`excludeFromContext?`: boolean | Run a shell command as the user would with `!`; `excludeFromContext` keeps its output out of the model context. The response data carries what the model gets: `header` (`[exit 0 · 4.2s · 312 lines · 18 KB]`, with what was trimmed and the full-output path when the output exceeded the `bashOutputMaxBytes` budget), the trimmed `output`, `totalLines`, `totalBytes` and `wallTimeSeconds`. |
| `abort_bash` |  | Stop a command started with `bash`. |
| `get_session_stats` |  | Token, cost and message statistics for the session. |
| `persist_session` |  | Write the session file now; fails when persistence is disabled. |
| `export_html` | `outputPath?`: string | Export the session to HTML; `data.path` is the written file. |
| `switch_session` | `sessionPath`: string | Open another session file. Fails, naming the pid, when another Octocode process has it open: two processes appending to one session overwrite each other's history. |
| `fork` | `entryId`: string | Fork from a user message entry; `data.text` is that message. |
| `clone` |  | Copy the current branch into a new session. |
| `get_fork_messages` |  | List user messages that can be forked from. |
| `get_entries` | `since?`: string | Session entries, or those after the entry id given in `since`. |
| `get_tree` |  | The session tree and current leaf. |
| `get_last_assistant_text` |  | Text of the last assistant message, or `null`. |
| `set_session_name` | `name`: string | Set the display name; empty names are refused. |
| `delete_sessions` | `sessionIds`: string[] | Delete saved sessions by id: transcript (to the trash when available), session folders and database rows, as the `/resume` picker does. The current session and sessions another process runs come back in `data.refused`; unknown ids in `data.notFound`. |
| `purge` | `scope`: "workspace" \| "all"<br>`confirm`: boolean | Delete this workspace's (`workspace`) or every workspace's and the global (`all`) Octocode data, as `/purge` does. `confirm` is required: `false` deletes nothing and returns the preview in `data.lines`; `true` deletes unless another live Octocode process holds sessions in scope (`data.refused` names it). The current session, settings, credentials and MCP configuration stay. |
| `get_messages` |  | The message history. |
| `get_commands` |  | Extension commands (with `argumentHint` when set), prompt templates and skill commands that a `prompt` can invoke. |
